17	def create_app(testing: bool = False) -> Flask:
18	    """Application factory.

23	    Returns:
24	        Configured Flask application instance.
25	    """
26	    app = Flask(__name__)
27	
28	    # --- Configuration ---

30	        app.config["SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI"] = "sqlite:///:memory:"
31	        app.config["TESTING"] = True
32	    else:

102	def _register_error_handlers(app: Flask) -> None:
103	    """Register global JSON error handlers."""
104	
105	    @app.errorhandler(400)
106	    def bad_request(exc):
107	        return _error_envelope("BAD_REQUEST", str(exc), 400)
108	
109	    @app.errorhandler(401)
110	    def unauthorized(exc):
111	        return _error_envelope("UNAUTHORIZED", "Authentication required.", 401)
112	
113	    @app.errorhandler(403)
114	    def forbidden(exc):
115	        return _error_envelope("FORBIDDEN", "Insufficient permissions.", 403)
116	
117	    @app.errorhandler(404)
118	    def not_found(exc):
119	        return _error_envelope("NOT_FOUND", "Resource not found.", 404)
120	
121	    @app.errorhandler(405)
122	    def method_not_allowed(exc):
123	        return _error_envelope("METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED", "Method not allowed.", 405)
124	
125	    @app.errorhandler(409)
126	    def conflict(exc):
127	        return _error_envelope("CONFLICT", str(exc), 409)
128	
129	    @app.errorhandler(422)
130	    def unprocessable(exc):
131	        return _error_envelope("UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY", str(exc), 422)
132	
133	    @app.errorhandler(429)
134	    def too_many_requests(exc):
135	        return _error_envelope("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "Rate limit exceeded.", 429)
136	
137	    @app.errorhandler(500)
138	    def internal_error(exc):
139	        logger.error("app", "unhandled", f"Internal server error: {exc}")
140	        return _error_envelope("INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", "An unexpected error occurred.", 500)

143	def _error_envelope(code: str, message: str, status_code: int):
144	    """Build a standard JSON error response."""
145	    body = {
146	        "error": {
147	            "code": code,
148	            "message": message,
149	        },
150	        "meta": {
151	            "request_id": getattr(g, "request_id", None),
152	            "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
153	        },
154	    }
155	    return jsonify(body), status_code

158	def _register_before_request(app: Flask) -> None:
159	    """Register before-request hooks."""
160	
161	    @app.before_request
162	    def assign_request_id():
163	        g.request_id = request.headers.get("X-Request-ID", str(uuid.uuid4()))
164	
165	    @app.before_request
166	    def enforce_tls():
167	        """Reject non-HTTPS requests when TLS is enabled."""
168	        if app.config.get("TESTING"):
169	            return None
170	        if not config.ENABLE_TLS:
171	            return None
172	        # X-Forwarded-Proto is set by reverse proxies; also check wsgi scheme
173	        proto = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-Proto", request.scheme)
174	        if proto != "https":
175	            logger.warning("security", "tls", f"Non-HTTPS request rejected: {request.url}")
176	            return _error_envelope("TLS_REQUIRED", "HTTPS is required.", 403)
177	
178	    @app.before_request
179	    def enforce_request_signing():
180	        """Verify request signature on every non-exempt request."""
181	        if app.config.get("TESTING"):
182	            return None
183	        if any(request.path.startswith(p) for p in SIGNING_EXEMPT_PREFIXES):
184	            return None
185	        is_valid, error_code = verify_request_signature(request)
186	        if not is_valid:
187	            logger.warning("security", "signing", f"Request signing failed: {error_code}")
188	            return _error_envelope("SIGNATURE_INVALID", f"Request signature validation failed: {error_code}", 401)
189	
190	    @app.before_request
191	    def enforce_rate_limit():
192	        """Apply rate limiting on every non-exempt request."""
193	        if app.config.get("TESTING"):
194	            return None
195	        if any(request.path.startswith(p) for p in RATE_LIMIT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES):
196	            return None
197	        # Use IP + path as the bucket key for unauthenticated requests
198	        bucket_key = f"ip:{request.remote_addr}"
199	        allowed, headers = check_rate_limit(
200	            bucket_key,
201	            max_tokens=config.RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE,
202	            refill_rate=config.RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE,
203	        )
204	        if not allowed:
205	            resp = _error_envelope("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "Rate limit exceeded.", 429)
206	            # resp is (json_response, status_code) tuple
207	            response = resp[0] if isinstance(resp, tuple) else resp
208	            for k, v in headers.items():
209	                response.headers[k] = v
210	            return resp
211	
212	    @app.before_request
213	    def log_request():
214	        logger.info(
215	            "http", "request",
216	            f"{request.method} {request.path}",
217	            request_id=g.request_id,
218	            remote_addr=request.remote_addr,
219	        )
220	
221	
222	def _register_after_request(app: Flask) -> None:
223	    """Register after-request hooks."""
224	
225	    @app.after_request
226	    def log_response(response):
227	        logger.info(
228	            "http", "response",
229	            f"{request.method} {request.path} -> {response.status_code}",
230	            request_id=getattr(g, "request_id", None),
231	        )
232	        return response
233	
234	    @app.after_request
235	    def set_security_headers(response):
236	        response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
237	        response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
238	        response.headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
239	
240	        # No-store for sensitive routes
241	        if any(request.path.startswith(prefix) for prefix in SENSITIVE_ROUTE_PREFIXES):
242	            response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
243	
244	        return response
245

247	def _create_overlap_index() -> None:
248	    """Create a partial unique index to prevent duplicate active reservations at DB level."""
249	    from sqlalchemy import text
250	    try:
251	        db.session.execute(text("""
252	            CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uix_reservation_no_overlap
253	            ON reservations (resource_id, start_time, end_time)
254	            WHERE status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
255	        """))
256	        db.session.commit()
257	    except Exception:
258	        db.session.rollback()

262	    """Create the default platform admin if no users exist yet."""
263	    from src.models.models import User
264	    from src.models.enums import RoleType
265	
266	    if User.query.first() is not None:
267	        return
268	
269	    from src.security.passwords import hash_password
270	
271	    admin_username = getattr(config, "ADMIN_USERNAME", None) or "admin"
272	    admin_password = getattr(config, "ADMIN_PASSWORD", None) or "admin"
273	
274	    admin = User(
275	        username=admin_username,
276	        password_hash=hash_password(admin_password),
277	        display_name="Platform Administrator",
278	        role=RoleType.PLATFORM_ADMIN.value,
279	        is_active=True,

281	    db.session.add(admin)
282	    db.session.commit()
283	    logger.info("app", "bootstrap", f"Platform admin created: {admin_username}")

100	    def __init__(self):
101	        """Load all configuration from environment variables with type-safe defaults."""
102	        for attr_name in dir(self):
103	            if attr_name.startswith("_") or attr_name != attr_name.upper():
104	                continue
105	            default = getattr(self, attr_name)
106	            env_val = os.environ.get(attr_name)
107	            if env_val is not None:
108	                if isinstance(default, bool):
109	                    setattr(self, attr_name, env_val.lower() in ("true", "1", "yes"))
110	                elif isinstance(default, int):
111	                    setattr(self, attr_name, int(env_val))
112	                elif isinstance(default, float):
113	                    setattr(self, attr_name, float(env_val))
114	                else:
115	                    setattr(self, attr_name, env_val)
116	
117	    def as_dict(self, redacted: bool = False) -> dict:
118	        """Return config as dict, optionally with secrets redacted."""
119	        sensitive_keys = {
120	            "SECRET_KEY", "JWT_SECRET_KEY", "ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY",
121	            "REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET", "DATABASE_URL"
122	        }
123	        result = {}
124	        for attr_name in sorted(dir(self)):
125	            if attr_name.startswith("_") or attr_name != attr_name.upper():
126	                continue
127	            val = getattr(self, attr_name)
128	            if redacted and attr_name in sensitive_keys:
129	                result[attr_name] = "***REDACTED***"
130	            else:
131	                result[attr_name] = val
132	        return result
133

25	def _get_user_permissions(user_id: str, org_id: str) -> list:
26	    """Load effective permission codes for a user in an org context."""
27	    from src.models.models import Permission, UserPermission
28	    query = db.session.query(Permission.code).join(
29	        UserPermission, UserPermission.permission_id == Permission.id
30	    ).filter(
31	        UserPermission.user_id == user_id,
32	    )
33	    if org_id:
34	        query = query.filter(
35	            db.or_(
36	                UserPermission.organization_id == org_id,
37	                UserPermission.organization_id.is_(None),
38	            ),
39	        )
40	    else:
41	        # No org context: load unscoped permissions only
42	        query = query.filter(UserPermission.organization_id.is_(None))
43	    return [r.code for r in query.all()]

17	    """Decorator that requires a valid JWT Bearer token.
18	
19	    Extracts the token from the Authorization header, decodes it, checks
20	    it is not in the denylist, and populates g.current_user with user info.
21	    """
22	    @functools.wraps(f)
23	    def decorated(*args, **kwargs):
24	        auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
25	        if not auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
26	            logger.warning("security", "auth", "Missing or malformed Authorization header")
27	            return error_response("UNAUTHORIZED", "Missing or invalid authorization header", status_code=401)
28

39	            return error_response("TOKEN_REVOKED", "Token has been revoked", status_code=401)

13	    max_tokens: int = 60,
14	    refill_rate: int = 60,
15	) -> tuple:
16	    """Check and consume a token from the rate limit bucket.
17	
18	    Uses a token bucket algorithm with per-minute refill. Each call consumes
19	    one token if available.
20	
21	    Args:
22	        bucket_key: Unique identifier for the rate limit bucket (e.g., "user:123", "ip:10.0.0.1").
23	        max_tokens: Maximum number of tokens the bucket can hold (burst capacity).
24	        refill_rate: Number of tokens added per minute.
25	
26	    Returns:
27	        Tuple of (allowed: bool, headers: dict) where headers contains:
28	            X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After.
29	    """
30	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
31	
32	    bucket = RateLimitBucket.query.filter_by(bucket_key=bucket_key).first()
33	
34	    if bucket is None:
35	        # Create a new bucket with full tokens minus the one being consumed
36	        bucket = RateLimitBucket(
37	            bucket_key=bucket_key,
38	            tokens=max_tokens - 1,
39	            last_refill_at=now,
40	        )
41	        db.session.add(bucket)
42	        db.session.commit()
43	
44	        headers = _build_headers(max_tokens, max_tokens - 1, now)
45	        logger.debug("security", "rate_limiter", f"New bucket created: {bucket_key}")
46	        return True, headers
47	
48	    # Calculate tokens to refill based on elapsed time
49	    elapsed_seconds = (now - bucket.last_refill_at).total_seconds()
50	    elapsed_minutes = elapsed_seconds / 60.0
51	    tokens_to_add = int(elapsed_minutes * refill_rate)
52	
53	    if tokens_to_add > 0:
54	        bucket.tokens = min(max_tokens, bucket.tokens + tokens_to_add)
55	        bucket.last_refill_at = now
56

58	        bucket.tokens -= 1
59	        db.session.commit()
60	
61	        headers = _build_headers(max_tokens, bucket.tokens, now)
62	        logger.debug("security", "rate_limiter", f"Token consumed: {bucket_key}, remaining={bucket.tokens}")

13	def create_access_token(
14	    user_id: str,
15	    username: str,
16	    role: str,
17	    organization_id: str = None,
18	    permissions: list = None,
19	) -> str:
20	    """Create a JWT access token with user claims.
21	
22	    Args:
23	        user_id: The user's unique identifier.
24	        username: The user's username.
25	        role: The user's role.
26	        organization_id: Optional organization context.
27	        permissions: Optional list of permission codes.
28	
29	    Returns:
30	        Encoded JWT string.
31	    """
32	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
33	    payload = {
34	        "sub": user_id,
35	        "username": username,
36	        "role": role,
37	        "org_id": organization_id,
38	        "permissions": permissions or [],
39	        "jti": str(uuid4()),
40	        "iat": now,
41	        "exp": now + timedelta(minutes=config.JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_MINUTES),
42	        "iss": config.JWT_ISSUER,
43	    }
44	    token = jwt.encode(payload, config.JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithm=config.JWT_ALGORITHM)
45	    logger.info("security", "tokens", f"Access token created for user={user_id}")
46	    return token
47	
48	
49	def create_refresh_token(user_id: str) -> str:
50	    """Create a JWT refresh token.
51	
52	    Args:
53	        user_id: The user's unique identifier.
54	
55	    Returns:
56	        Encoded JWT refresh token string.
57	    """
58	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
59	    payload = {
60	        "sub": user_id,
61	        "jti": str(uuid4()),
62	        "type": "refresh",
63	        "iat": now,
64	        "exp": now + timedelta(days=config.JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS),
65	        "iss": config.JWT_ISSUER,
66	    }
67	    token = jwt.encode(payload, config.JWT_SECRET_KEY, algorithm=config.JWT_ALGORITHM)
68	    logger.info("security", "tokens", f"Refresh token created for user={user_id}")
69	    return token
70	
71	
72	def decode_token(token: str) -> dict | None:
73	    """Decode and validate a JWT token.
74	
75	    Args:
76	        token: The encoded JWT string.
77	
78	    Returns:
79	        The decoded payload dict, or None if decoding/validation fails.
80	    """
81	    try:
82	        payload = jwt.decode(
83	            token,
84	            config.JWT_SECRET_KEY,
85	            algorithms=[config.JWT_ALGORITHM],
86	            issuer=config.JWT_ISSUER,
87	        )
88	        return payload
89	    except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
90	        logger.warning("security", "tokens", "Token has expired")

92	    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
93	        logger.warning("security", "tokens", f"Invalid token: {exc}")

1	# Security Model
2	
3	Describes all security controls, where they are enforced, and boundaries that require manual verification.
4	
5	## 1. Authentication
6	
7	### JWT Token Lifecycle
8	
9	- **Algorithm**: HS256 (configurable via `JWT_ALGORITHM`)
10	- **Access token TTL**: 30 minutes (configurable via `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_MINUTES`)
11	- **Refresh token TTL**: 14 days (configurable via `JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS`)
12	- **Issuer claim**: `learning-booking-api` (configurable via `JWT_ISSUER`)
13	- **Enforcement**: `src/security/auth_middleware.py` (`require_auth` decorator)
14	- **Token rotation**: Refresh endpoint revokes the old refresh token and issues a new pair
15	- **Denylist**: Logout places access token JTI on `access_token_denylist` table; middleware checks before granting access
16	- **Refresh token storage**: Only SHA-256 hash stored in `refresh_tokens` table, raw token never persisted
17	
18	### Login Lockout
19	
20	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py`
21	- **Threshold**: 5 failures triggers lockout (configurable via `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES`)
22	- **Duration**: 15 minutes (configurable via `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES`)
23	- **Tracking**: `login_failure_counters` table keyed by username
24	- **Reset**: Counter resets on successful login
25	
26	### CAPTCHA Challenge
27	
28	- **Trigger**: After 3 failed attempts (configurable via `CAPTCHA_THRESHOLD`)
29	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py` generates a math-based challenge stored in `login_challenges` table
30	- **Enforcement**: `src/api/auth.py` login endpoint checks `needs_captcha()` before credential verification
31	- **Expiry**: Challenge records expire and are single-use (`is_solved` flag)
32	
33	### Device Fingerprint Blacklisting
34	
35	- **Storage**: `devices` table with `fingerprint_hash` (AES-256-GCM encrypted) and `fingerprint_lookup_hash` (HMAC-SHA256 deterministic)
36	- **Blacklist check**: Login endpoint queries `fingerprint_lookup_hash` for `BLACKLISTED` status
37	- **Retry window**: 168 hours / 7 days (configurable via `DEVICE_BLACKLIST_RETRY_AFTER_HOURS`)
38	- **Risk score threshold**: 0.9 (configurable via `DEVICE_RISK_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD`)
39	
40	## 2. Authorization (RBAC)
41	
42	### Role Hierarchy
43	
44	| Level | Role | Scope |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| 3 | `platform_admin` | Full system access |
47	| 2 | `org_admin` | Organization-scoped management |
48	| 1 | `member` | Standard authenticated user |
49	| 0 | `guest` | Minimal access, self-registered |
50	
51	- **Enforcement**: `require_role()` decorator in `src/security/auth_middleware.py`
52	- **Hierarchy rule**: A caller can only manage users/permissions at or below their own role level
53	- **Org boundary**: Non-platform-admins are scoped to their organization via `Membership` table
54	
55	### Permission System
56	
57	- **Model**: `permissions` defines permission codes; `user_permissions` assigns them per user per org
58	- **Enforcement**: `require_permission()` decorator checks JWT claims at request time
59	- **Claim embedding**: Permission codes are embedded in the access token at login/refresh
60	
61	## 3. Transport Security
62	
63	### TLS Enforcement
64	
65	- **Toggle**: `ENABLE_TLS` config flag (default: `true`)
66	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py` checks `X-Forwarded-Proto` or `request.scheme`
67	- **Response**: 403 `TLS_REQUIRED` if non-HTTPS detected
68	- **Certificate paths**: `/app/certs/cert.pem`, `/app/certs/key.pem`
69	
70	### Request Signing (HMAC-SHA256)
71	
72	- **Implementation**: `src/security/signing.py`
73	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
74	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
75	- **Clock skew tolerance**: +/- 300 seconds (configurable via `REQUEST_SIGNING_SKEW_SECONDS`)
76	- **Nonce replay protection**: `nonce_store` table, retention 600 seconds (configurable via `NONCE_RETENTION_SECONDS`)
77	
78	### Security Response Headers
79	
80	Set in `after_request` hook in `src/app.py`:
81	- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
82	- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
83	- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
84	- `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/auth` and `/admin` routes
85	
86	## 4. Rate Limiting
87	
88	- **Algorithm**: Token bucket
89	- **Implementation**: `src/security/rate_limiter.py`, state in `rate_limit_buckets` table
90	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
91	- **Default rate**: 60 requests/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE`)
92	- **Burst**: 20 tokens (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`)
93	- **Bucket key**: `ip:<remote_addr>` for unauthenticated requests
94	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
95	- **Response**: 429 with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers
96	
97	## 5. Encryption at Rest
98	
99	- **Algorithm**: AES-256-GCM via `cryptography` library
100	- **Key derivation**: HKDF-SHA256 from `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` with context-specific info strings
101	- **Implementation**: `src/security/encryption.py`
102	- **SQLAlchemy integration**: `EncryptedText` custom type in `src/models/models.py`
103	- **Encrypted fields**: `moderation_cases.decision_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_decision_notes`
104	- **Device fingerprint**: Encrypted via AES-256-GCM for storage, HMAC-SHA256 for deterministic lookup
105	
106	## 6. Audit Trail
107	
108	- **Table**: `audit_events` (insert-only, no update/delete endpoints exposed)
109	- **Coverage**: All auth events, permission changes, booking state transitions, content actions, moderation decisions, export/backup operations
110	- **Fields**: `event_type`, `actor_id`, `actor_ip`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `organization_id`, `before_state`, `after_state`
111	- **Alert integration**: `alerts` table with severity levels, auto-generated on login failure spikes and booking conflict spikes
112	
113	## 7. Manual Verification Boundaries
114	
115	These controls depend on deployment configuration and cannot be fully verified by automated tests:
116	
117	| Control | What to Verify |
118	|---|---|
119	| TLS certificate | Valid cert chain, strong cipher suite, no expired certs |
120	| Encryption master key | Production key is >= 32 bytes, stored in secret manager, not in source control |
121	| Signing secret | Production secret differs from defaults, rotated periodically |
122	| JWT secret key | Production key differs from default, sufficient entropy |
123	| Database file permissions | SQLite file not world-readable; or use PostgreSQL with auth in production |
124	| Backup encryption | Backup files at `/app/backups` are access-controlled and optionally encrypted |
125	| Container isolation | Docker volumes for data, exports, backups are not exposed to host unnecessarily |
126	| Rate limiter tuning | Thresholds appropriate for production traffic patterns |
127	
128	## 8. Booking Overlap — SQLite Concurrency Strategy
129	
130	SQLite cannot enforce general interval exclusion constraints at the DB level (that requires
131	range exclusion operators only available in PostgreSQL). The booking engine uses a three-layer
132	defence to prevent double-booking / overselling:
133	
134	1. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — issued before the overlap check in `src/api/booking.py` (`create_hold`).
135	   This acquires an exclusive write lock on the database so the read-check-then-insert sequence
136	   is atomic with respect to other writers. Any concurrent writer blocks until the transaction
137	   commits or rolls back.
138	
139	2. **Application-level interval intersection query** — `_check_overlap()` uses the standard
140	   interval overlap predicate (`existing.start_time < new.end_time AND existing.end_time > new.start_time`,
141	   with configurable buffer) to detect conflicts among `HELD` and `CONFIRMED` reservations.
142	   This catches partial overlaps (e.g. 10:00–11:00 vs 10:30–11:30), not just exact duplicates.
143	
144	3. **Partial unique index + `IntegrityError` catch** — a unique index on
145	   `(resource_id, start_time, end_time) WHERE status IN ('HELD','CONFIRMED')` acts as a
146	   safety net for the exact-duplicate race. The `IntegrityError` handler in the hold endpoint
147	   rolls back and returns `409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
148	
149	**Migration to PostgreSQL**: When moving to PostgreSQL, replace layers 1 and 3 with an
150	`EXCLUDE USING gist` constraint on `(resource_id WITH =, tstzrange(start_time, end_time) WITH &&)`
151	and remove the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` call (PostgreSQL uses MVCC, not file-level locking).
152	The application-level check (layer 2) can remain as a user-friendly pre-check.

1	# Security Model
2	
3	Describes all security controls, where they are enforced, and boundaries that require manual verification.
4	
5	## 1. Authentication
6	
7	### JWT Token Lifecycle
8	
9	- **Algorithm**: HS256 (configurable via `JWT_ALGORITHM`)
10	- **Access token TTL**: 30 minutes (configurable via `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_MINUTES`)
11	- **Refresh token TTL**: 14 days (configurable via `JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS`)
12	- **Issuer claim**: `learning-booking-api` (configurable via `JWT_ISSUER`)
13	- **Enforcement**: `src/security/auth_middleware.py` (`require_auth` decorator)
14	- **Token rotation**: Refresh endpoint revokes the old refresh token and issues a new pair
15	- **Denylist**: Logout places access token JTI on `access_token_denylist` table; middleware checks before granting access
16	- **Refresh token storage**: Only SHA-256 hash stored in `refresh_tokens` table, raw token never persisted
17	
18	### Login Lockout
19	
20	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py`
21	- **Threshold**: 5 failures triggers lockout (configurable via `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES`)
22	- **Duration**: 15 minutes (configurable via `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES`)
23	- **Tracking**: `login_failure_counters` table keyed by username
24	- **Reset**: Counter resets on successful login
25	
26	### CAPTCHA Challenge
27	
28	- **Trigger**: After 3 failed attempts (configurable via `CAPTCHA_THRESHOLD`)
29	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py` generates a math-based challenge stored in `login_challenges` table
30	- **Enforcement**: `src/api/auth.py` login endpoint checks `needs_captcha()` before credential verification
31	- **Expiry**: Challenge records expire and are single-use (`is_solved` flag)
32	
33	### Device Fingerprint Blacklisting
34	
35	- **Storage**: `devices` table with `fingerprint_hash` (AES-256-GCM encrypted) and `fingerprint_lookup_hash` (HMAC-SHA256 deterministic)
36	- **Blacklist check**: Login endpoint queries `fingerprint_lookup_hash` for `BLACKLISTED` status
37	- **Retry window**: 168 hours / 7 days (configurable via `DEVICE_BLACKLIST_RETRY_AFTER_HOURS`)
38	- **Risk score threshold**: 0.9 (configurable via `DEVICE_RISK_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD`)
39	
40	## 2. Authorization (RBAC)
41	
42	### Role Hierarchy
43	
44	| Level | Role | Scope |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| 3 | `platform_admin` | Full system access |
47	| 2 | `org_admin` | Organization-scoped management |
48	| 1 | `member` | Standard authenticated user |
49	| 0 | `guest` | Minimal access, self-registered |
50	
51	- **Enforcement**: `require_role()` decorator in `src/security/auth_middleware.py`
52	- **Hierarchy rule**: A caller can only manage users/permissions at or below their own role level
53	- **Org boundary**: Non-platform-admins are scoped to their organization via `Membership` table
54	
55	### Permission System
56	
57	- **Model**: `permissions` defines permission codes; `user_permissions` assigns them per user per org
58	- **Enforcement**: `require_permission()` decorator checks JWT claims at request time
59	- **Claim embedding**: Permission codes are embedded in the access token at login/refresh
60	
61	## 3. Transport Security
62	
63	### TLS Enforcement
64	
65	- **Toggle**: `ENABLE_TLS` config flag (default: `true`)
66	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py` checks `X-Forwarded-Proto` or `request.scheme`
67	- **Response**: 403 `TLS_REQUIRED` if non-HTTPS detected
68	- **Certificate paths**: `/app/certs/cert.pem`, `/app/certs/key.pem`
69	
70	### Request Signing (HMAC-SHA256)
71	
72	- **Implementation**: `src/security/signing.py`
73	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
74	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
75	- **Clock skew tolerance**: +/- 300 seconds (configurable via `REQUEST_SIGNING_SKEW_SECONDS`)
76	- **Nonce replay protection**: `nonce_store` table, retention 600 seconds (configurable via `NONCE_RETENTION_SECONDS`)
77	
78	### Security Response Headers
79	
80	Set in `after_request` hook in `src/app.py`:
81	- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
82	- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
83	- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
84	- `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/auth` and `/admin` routes
85	
86	## 4. Rate Limiting
87	
88	- **Algorithm**: Token bucket
89	- **Implementation**: `src/security/rate_limiter.py`, state in `rate_limit_buckets` table
90	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
91	- **Default rate**: 60 requests/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE`)
92	- **Burst**: 20 tokens (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`)
93	- **Bucket key**: `ip:<remote_addr>` for unauthenticated requests
94	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
95	- **Response**: 429 with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers
96	
97	## 5. Encryption at Rest
98	
99	- **Algorithm**: AES-256-GCM via `cryptography` library
100	- **Key derivation**: HKDF-SHA256 from `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` with context-specific info strings
101	- **Implementation**: `src/security/encryption.py`
102	- **SQLAlchemy integration**: `EncryptedText` custom type in `src/models/models.py`
103	- **Encrypted fields**: `moderation_cases.decision_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_decision_notes`
104	- **Device fingerprint**: Encrypted via AES-256-GCM for storage, HMAC-SHA256 for deterministic lookup
105	
106	## 6. Audit Trail
107	
108	- **Table**: `audit_events` (insert-only, no update/delete endpoints exposed)
109	- **Coverage**: All auth events, permission changes, booking state transitions, content actions, moderation decisions, export/backup operations
110	- **Fields**: `event_type`, `actor_id`, `actor_ip`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `organization_id`, `before_state`, `after_state`
111	- **Alert integration**: `alerts` table with severity levels, auto-generated on login failure spikes and booking conflict spikes
112	
113	## 7. Manual Verification Boundaries
114	
115	These controls depend on deployment configuration and cannot be fully verified by automated tests:
116	
117	| Control | What to Verify |
118	|---|---|
119	| TLS certificate | Valid cert chain, strong cipher suite, no expired certs |
120	| Encryption master key | Production key is >= 32 bytes, stored in secret manager, not in source control |
121	| Signing secret | Production secret differs from defaults, rotated periodically |
122	| JWT secret key | Production key differs from default, sufficient entropy |
123	| Database file permissions | SQLite file not world-readable; or use PostgreSQL with auth in production |
124	| Backup encryption | Backup files at `/app/backups` are access-controlled and optionally encrypted |
125	| Container isolation | Docker volumes for data, exports, backups are not exposed to host unnecessarily |
126	| Rate limiter tuning | Thresholds appropriate for production traffic patterns |
127	
128	## 8. Booking Overlap — SQLite Concurrency Strategy
129	
130	SQLite cannot enforce general interval exclusion constraints at the DB level (that requires
131	range exclusion operators only available in PostgreSQL). The booking engine uses a three-layer
132	defence to prevent double-booking / overselling:
133	
134	1. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — issued before the overlap check in `src/api/booking.py` (`create_hold`).
135	   This acquires an exclusive write lock on the database so the read-check-then-insert sequence
136	   is atomic with respect to other writers. Any concurrent writer blocks until the transaction
137	   commits or rolls back.
138	
139	2. **Application-level interval intersection query** — `_check_overlap()` uses the standard
140	   interval overlap predicate (`existing.start_time < new.end_time AND existing.end_time > new.start_time`,
141	   with configurable buffer) to detect conflicts among `HELD` and `CONFIRMED` reservations.
142	   This catches partial overlaps (e.g. 10:00–11:00 vs 10:30–11:30), not just exact duplicates.
143	
144	3. **Partial unique index + `IntegrityError` catch** — a unique index on
145	   `(resource_id, start_time, end_time) WHERE status IN ('HELD','CONFIRMED')` acts as a
146	   safety net for the exact-duplicate race. The `IntegrityError` handler in the hold endpoint
147	   rolls back and returns `409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
148	
149	**Migration to PostgreSQL**: When moving to PostgreSQL, replace layers 1 and 3 with an
150	`EXCLUDE USING gist` constraint on `(resource_id WITH =, tstzrange(start_time, end_time) WITH &&)`
151	and remove the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` call (PostgreSQL uses MVCC, not file-level locking).
152	The application-level check (layer 2) can remain as a user-friendly pre-check.

    def enforce_rate_limit():
        """Apply rate limiting on every non-exempt request.

        Uses IP-based bucket for all requests. For authenticated requests
        (Bearer token present), also enforces a per-identity bucket keyed
        by user ID.
        """
        if app.config.get("TESTING"):
            return None
        if any(request.path.startswith(p) for p in RATE_LIMIT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES):
            return None

        # IP-based rate limit for all requests
        bucket_key = f"ip:{request.remote_addr}"
        allowed, headers = check_rate_limit(
            bucket_key,
            max_tokens=config.RATE_LIMIT_BURST,
            refill_rate=config.RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE,
        )
        if not allowed:
            resp = _error_envelope("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", "Rate limit exceeded.", 429)
            response = resp[0] if isinstance(resp, tuple) else resp
            for k, v in headers.items():
                response.headers[k] = v
            return resp

        auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")

                    user_bucket_key,
                    max_tokens=config.RATE_LIMIT_BURST,
                    refill_rate=config.RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE,
                )

276	
277	## Security Model Summary
278	
279	- **Password hashing**: Argon2id with per-user salt
280	- **Encryption at rest**: AES-256-GCM with HKDF-SHA256 key derivation and per-field IV
281	- **JWT authentication**: Access and refresh tokens with rotation and revocation
282	- **Request signing**: HMAC-SHA256 over method, path, timestamp, nonce, and body hash
283	- **Rate limiting**: Per-IP and per-identity buckets with configurable burst allowance
284	- **Login security**: Account lockout after configurable failed attempts; captcha challenge gate
285	- **Role-based access control**: 4-tier hierarchy (guest, member, org_admin, platform_admin) with least-privilege defaults
286	- **Object-level authorization**: Ownership and org-scope checks on every loaded resource
287	- **Tenant isolation**: All queries constrained by organization context unless platform_admin
288

290	
291	## Known Limitations and Manual Verification Boundaries
292	
293	- **SQLite single-writer limitation**: SQLite does not support true concurrent writes. Write serialization is enforced via `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions.
294	- **Hold auto-release depends on scheduler**: The hold expiry job must be running for automatic release. Testable with manual time manipulation in unit tests.
295	- **TLS certificate generation requires openssl on host**: The cert generation scripts depend on `openssl` being available in the host environment.
296	- **Backup scheduler tested via unit test**: Runtime cron execution verification is manual. The backup job logic is covered by unit tests, but actual scheduled execution in Docker requires manual observation.
297	- **Export CSV generation is synchronous**: Suitable for moderate dataset sizes. Large exports may block the request thread.
298	- **No email/SMS delivery**: Invitation codes are returned directly in the API response. There is no external notification mechanism.

    """Create DB-level overlap prevention for reservations.

    Layer 1: Partial unique index prevents exact-duplicate (resource, start, end).
    Layer 2: BEFORE INSERT trigger rejects any new HELD/CONFIRMED reservation
             whose time range overlaps an existing HELD/CONFIRMED reservation on
             the same resource.  This closes the gap that the unique index alone
             cannot cover (partial overlaps like 10:00-11:00 vs 10:30-11:30).
    """
    from sqlalchemy import text
    try:
        # Keep the exact-duplicate safety net
        db.session.execute(text("""
            CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uix_reservation_no_overlap
            ON reservations (resource_id, start_time, end_time)
            WHERE status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
        """))

        # Trigger-based overlap rejection for INSERT
        db.session.execute(text("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_reservation_no_overlap_insert
            BEFORE INSERT ON reservations
            WHEN NEW.status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'OVERLAP_CONFLICT: reservation overlaps an existing active reservation')
                WHERE EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM reservations
                    WHERE resource_id = NEW.resource_id
                      AND status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
                      AND start_time < NEW.end_time
                      AND end_time > NEW.start_time
                );
            END
        """))

        # Trigger-based overlap rejection for UPDATE (e.g. reschedule)
        db.session.execute(text("""
            CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS trg_reservation_no_overlap_update
            BEFORE UPDATE ON reservations
            WHEN NEW.status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
            BEGIN
                SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'OVERLAP_CONFLICT: reservation overlaps an existing active reservation')
                WHERE EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1 FROM reservations
                    WHERE resource_id = NEW.resource_id
                      AND id != NEW.id
                      AND status IN ('HELD', 'CONFIRMED')
                      AND start_time < NEW.end_time
                      AND end_time > NEW.start_time
                );
            END
        """))

        db.session.commit()
    except Exception:
        db.session.rollback()"}

175	        if current_user.role != RoleType.PLATFORM_ADMIN.value:

1	# Security Model
2	
3	Describes all security controls, where they are enforced, and boundaries that require manual verification.
4	
5	## 1. Authentication
6	
7	### JWT Token Lifecycle
8	
9	- **Algorithm**: HS256 (configurable via `JWT_ALGORITHM`)
10	- **Access token TTL**: 30 minutes (configurable via `JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_MINUTES`)
11	- **Refresh token TTL**: 14 days (configurable via `JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS`)
12	- **Issuer claim**: `learning-booking-api` (configurable via `JWT_ISSUER`)
13	- **Enforcement**: `src/security/auth_middleware.py` (`require_auth` decorator)
14	- **Token rotation**: Refresh endpoint revokes the old refresh token and issues a new pair
15	- **Denylist**: Logout places access token JTI on `access_token_denylist` table; middleware checks before granting access
16	- **Refresh token storage**: Only SHA-256 hash stored in `refresh_tokens` table, raw token never persisted
17	
18	### Login Lockout
19	
20	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py`
21	- **Threshold**: 5 failures triggers lockout (configurable via `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES`)
22	- **Duration**: 15 minutes (configurable via `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES`)
23	- **Tracking**: `login_failure_counters` table keyed by username
24	- **Reset**: Counter resets on successful login
25	
26	### CAPTCHA Challenge
27	
28	- **Trigger**: After 3 failed attempts (configurable via `CAPTCHA_THRESHOLD`)
29	- **Implementation**: `src/security/lockout.py` generates a math-based challenge stored in `login_challenges` table
30	- **Enforcement**: `src/api/auth.py` login endpoint checks `needs_captcha()` before credential verification
31	- **Expiry**: Challenge records expire and are single-use (`is_solved` flag)
32	
33	### Device Fingerprint Blacklisting
34	
35	- **Storage**: `devices` table with `fingerprint_hash` (AES-256-GCM encrypted) and `fingerprint_lookup_hash` (HMAC-SHA256 deterministic)
36	- **Blacklist check**: Login endpoint queries `fingerprint_lookup_hash` for `BLACKLISTED` status
37	- **Retry window**: 168 hours / 7 days (configurable via `DEVICE_BLACKLIST_RETRY_AFTER_HOURS`)
38	- **Risk score threshold**: 0.9 (configurable via `DEVICE_RISK_BLACKLIST_THRESHOLD`)
39	
40	## 2. Authorization (RBAC)
41	
42	### Role Hierarchy
43	
44	| Level | Role | Scope |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| 3 | `platform_admin` | Full system access |
47	| 2 | `org_admin` | Organization-scoped management |
48	| 1 | `member` | Standard authenticated user |
49	| 0 | `guest` | Minimal access, self-registered |
50	
51	- **Enforcement**: `require_role()` decorator in `src/security/auth_middleware.py`
52	- **Hierarchy rule**: A caller can only manage users/permissions at or below their own role level
53	- **Org boundary**: Non-platform-admins are scoped to their organization via `Membership` table
54	
55	### Permission System
56	
57	- **Model**: `permissions` defines permission codes; `user_permissions` assigns them per user per org
58	- **Enforcement**: `require_permission()` decorator checks JWT claims at request time
59	- **Claim embedding**: Permission codes are embedded in the access token at login/refresh
60	
61	## 3. Transport Security
62	
63	### TLS Enforcement
64	
65	- **Toggle**: `ENABLE_TLS` config flag (default: `true`)
66	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py` checks `X-Forwarded-Proto` or `request.scheme`
67	- **Response**: 403 `TLS_REQUIRED` if non-HTTPS detected
68	- **Certificate paths**: `/app/certs/cert.pem`, `/app/certs/key.pem`
69	
70	### Request Signing (HMAC-SHA256)
71	
72	- **Implementation**: `src/security/signing.py`
73	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
74	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
75	- **Clock skew tolerance**: +/- 300 seconds (configurable via `REQUEST_SIGNING_SKEW_SECONDS`)
76	- **Nonce replay protection**: `nonce_store` table, retention 600 seconds (configurable via `NONCE_RETENTION_SECONDS`)
77	
78	### Security Response Headers
79	
80	Set in `after_request` hook in `src/app.py`:
81	- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
82	- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
83	- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
84	- `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/auth` and `/admin` routes
85	
86	## 4. Rate Limiting
87	
88	- **Algorithm**: Token bucket
89	- **Implementation**: `src/security/rate_limiter.py`, state in `rate_limit_buckets` table
90	- **Enforcement**: `before_request` hook in `src/app.py`
91	- **Default rate**: 60 requests/minute (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE`)
92	- **Burst**: 20 tokens (configurable via `RATE_LIMIT_BURST`)
93	- **Bucket key**: `ip:<remote_addr>` for unauthenticated requests
94	- **Exempt paths**: `/health`
95	- **Response**: 429 with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers
96	
97	## 5. Encryption at Rest
98	
99	- **Algorithm**: AES-256-GCM via `cryptography` library
100	- **Key derivation**: HKDF-SHA256 from `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` with context-specific info strings
101	- **Implementation**: `src/security/encryption.py`
102	- **SQLAlchemy integration**: `EncryptedText` custom type in `src/models/models.py`
103	- **Encrypted fields**: `moderation_cases.decision_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_notes`, `moderation_cases.appeal_decision_notes`
104	- **Device fingerprint**: Encrypted via AES-256-GCM for storage, HMAC-SHA256 for deterministic lookup
105	
106	## 6. Audit Trail
107	
108	- **Table**: `audit_events` (insert-only, no update/delete endpoints exposed)
109	- **Coverage**: All auth events, permission changes, booking state transitions, content actions, moderation decisions, export/backup operations
110	- **Fields**: `event_type`, `actor_id`, `actor_ip`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `organization_id`, `before_state`, `after_state`
111	- **Alert integration**: `alerts` table with severity levels, auto-generated on login failure spikes and booking conflict spikes
112	
113	## 7. Manual Verification Boundaries
114	
115	These controls depend on deployment configuration and cannot be fully verified by automated tests:
116	
117	| Control | What to Verify |
118	|---|---|
119	| TLS certificate | Valid cert chain, strong cipher suite, no expired certs |
120	| Encryption master key | Production key is >= 32 bytes, stored in secret manager, not in source control |
121	| Signing secret | Production secret differs from defaults, rotated periodically |
122	| JWT secret key | Production key differs from default, sufficient entropy |
123	| Database file permissions | SQLite file not world-readable; or use PostgreSQL with auth in production |
124	| Backup encryption | Backup files at `/app/backups` are access-controlled and optionally encrypted |
125	| Container isolation | Docker volumes for data, exports, backups are not exposed to host unnecessarily |
126	| Rate limiter tuning | Thresholds appropriate for production traffic patterns |
127	
128	## 8. Booking Overlap — SQLite Concurrency Strategy
129	
130	SQLite cannot enforce general interval exclusion constraints at the DB level (that requires
131	range exclusion operators only available in PostgreSQL). The booking engine uses a three-layer
132	defence to prevent double-booking / overselling:
133	
134	1. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** — issued before the overlap check in `src/api/booking.py` (`create_hold`).
135	   This acquires an exclusive write lock on the database so the read-check-then-insert sequence
136	   is atomic with respect to other writers. Any concurrent writer blocks until the transaction
137	   commits or rolls back.
138	
139	2. **Application-level interval intersection query** — `_check_overlap()` uses the standard
140	   interval overlap predicate (`existing.start_time < new.end_time AND existing.end_time > new.start_time`,
141	   with configurable buffer) to detect conflicts among `HELD` and `CONFIRMED` reservations.
142	   This catches partial overlaps (e.g. 10:00–11:00 vs 10:30–11:30), not just exact duplicates.
143	
144	3. **Partial unique index + `IntegrityError` catch** — a unique index on
145	   `(resource_id, start_time, end_time) WHERE status IN ('HELD','CONFIRMED')` acts as a
146	   safety net for the exact-duplicate race. The `IntegrityError` handler in the hold endpoint
147	   rolls back and returns `409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
148	
149	**Migration to PostgreSQL**: When moving to PostgreSQL, replace layers 1 and 3 with an
150	`EXCLUDE USING gist` constraint on `(resource_id WITH =, tstzrange(start_time, end_time) WITH &&)`
151	and remove the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` call (PostgreSQL uses MVCC, not file-level locking).
152	The application-level check (layer 2) can remain as a user-friendly pre-check.

1	# Operational Runbook
2	
3	Procedures for startup, migration, backup, recovery, and alert response.
4	
5	## 1. Application Startup
6	
7	### Prerequisites
8	- Docker and Docker Compose installed
9	- TLS certificates placed at `./certs/cert.pem` and `./certs/key.pem`
10	- Environment variables reviewed in `docker-compose.yml` (change all default secrets for production)
11	
12	### Start the service (Docker)
13	```
14	docker compose up -d
15	```
16	
17	### Start locally (development)
18	```
19	pip install -r src/requirements.txt
20	python -c "from src.app import create_app; app = create_app(); app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)"
21	```
22	
23	### Start with Gunicorn (production without Docker)
24	```
25	gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 --workers 1 --threads 4 'src.app:create_app()'
26	```
27	
28	### Verify startup
29	```
30	curl -k https://localhost:5000/health
31	```
32	Expected: `{"data": {"status": "healthy", "database": "connected", ...}}`
33	
34	### First boot behavior
35	- On first start with an empty database, `db.create_all()` creates all tables
36	- A default platform admin is bootstrapped (`ADMIN_USERNAME` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, defaults to admin/admin)
37	- Change the admin password immediately in production
38	
39	### Configuration
40	- All configuration flows through `src/config/__init__.py`
41	- Set environment variables to override defaults; never edit code for config changes
42	- Sensitive keys that must be changed for production: `SECRET_KEY`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`, `REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET`
43	
44	### TLS Certificate Generation (Development)
45	```
46	openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout certs/key.pem -out certs/cert.pem -days 365 -nodes
47	```
48	To disable TLS for local development, set `ENABLE_TLS=false`.
49	
50	## 2. Database Migration
51	
52	The application uses SQLAlchemy with `db.create_all()` for table creation. For schema changes:
53	
54	### Adding new columns or tables
55	1. Update model definitions in `src/models/models.py`
56	2. If using Alembic (recommended for production), generate a migration:
57	   ```
58	   alembic revision --autogenerate -m "description"
59	   alembic upgrade head
60	   ```
61	3. Without Alembic, the app calls `db.create_all()` on startup, which creates missing tables but does not alter existing ones
62	
63	### Breaking schema changes
64	1. Back up the database before applying changes (see section 3)
65	2. Apply migration during a maintenance window
66	3. Verify by hitting `/health` and `/admin/system-status`
67	
68	## 3. Backup Procedures
69	
70	### Configuration
71	- Backup directory: `/app/backups` (Docker volume `app-backups`)
72	- Retention: 14 days (configurable via `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS`)
73	- Schedule: Daily at 02:00 UTC (configurable via `BACKUP_SCHEDULE_CRON`)
74	
75	### Scheduled Jobs
76	
77	| Job | Interval | Description |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Hold auto-release | 1 min | Releases expired reservation holds |
80	| Nonce cleanup | 10 min | Removes expired nonces from signing store |
81	| Denylist cleanup | 1 hour | Removes expired access token denylist entries |
82	| Backup | Daily 2 AM | SQLite database backup |
83	| Backup purge | Daily 3 AM | Removes backups older than retention period |
84	| Idempotency cleanup | 6 hours | Removes expired idempotency records |
85	| Anomaly alerts | 5 min | Evaluates login failure spikes |
86	
87	### Manual backup (SQLite)
88	```
89	docker compose exec api cp /app/data/app.db /app/backups/app-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).db
90	```
91	
92	### Verify backup integrity
93	```
94	docker compose exec api sqlite3 /app/backups/<backup-file> "SELECT count(*) FROM users;"
95	```
96	
97	### Export data
98	The API supports CSV exports via `POST /exports`. Exported files are stored in `/app/exports` (Docker volume `app-exports`).
99	
100	### Backup retention cleanup
101	Old backups beyond `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS` should be removed by the scheduler or a cron job:
102	```
103	find /app/backups -name "*.db" -mtime +14 -delete
104	```
105	
106	## 4. Recovery Procedures
107	
108	### Restore from backup (SQLite)
109	1. Stop the service: `docker compose stop api`
110	2. Copy backup file over the database: `cp /app/backups/<backup-file> /app/data/app.db`
111	3. Restart: `docker compose start api`
112	4. Verify: `curl -k https://localhost:5000/health`
113	
114	### Recovery from corrupted database
115	1. Stop the service
116	2. Restore the most recent verified backup
117	3. Review `audit_events` to assess data loss window
118	4. Restart and verify
119	
120	### Recovery from lost encryption key
121	- If `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` is lost, encrypted fields (`moderation_cases.decision_notes`, `appeal_notes`, `appeal_decision_notes`, device fingerprints) cannot be decrypted
122	- The application will continue to function but those fields will return raw ciphertext
123	- There is no recovery path; key management is critical
124	
125	## 5. Alert Response Procedures
126	
127	### Alert severity levels
128	
129	| Severity | Response SLA | Examples |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| CRITICAL | Immediate | Backup failure |
132	| HIGH | Within 1 hour | Login failure spike (>=10 failures in 300s) |
133	| MEDIUM | Within 4 hours | Booking conflict spike on a resource |
134	| LOW | Next business day | (reserved for future use) |
135	
136	### FAILED_LOGIN_SPIKE alert
137	1. Check `GET /audit-events?event_type=USER_LOGIN_FAILED` for the affected time window
138	2. Identify if it is a single user (targeted attack) or multiple users (credential stuffing)
139	3. For single user: verify the account is locked, consider manual password reset
140	4. For multiple users: review source IPs, consider IP-level blocking at the reverse proxy
141	5. Acknowledge the alert: `POST /alerts/<id>/ack`
142	6. Resolve after mitigation: `POST /alerts/<id>/resolve`
143	
144	### BOOKING_CONFLICT_SPIKE alert
145	1. Check `GET /audit-events?event_type=RESERVATION_HELD` for the affected resource
146	2. Review whether the resource capacity or slot quotas need adjustment
147	3. If a single user is causing excessive holds, review for abuse
148	4. Acknowledge and resolve the alert
149	
150	### BACKUP_FAILURE alert
151	1. Check disk space on backup volume: `docker compose exec api df -h /app/backups`
152	2. Verify file permissions on backup directory
153	3. Check database connectivity via `/health`
154	4. Manually trigger a backup and verify success
155	5. Acknowledge and resolve the alert
156	
157	### General alert workflow
158	- View alerts: `GET /alerts?status=OPEN`
159	- Filter by severity: `GET /alerts?severity=HIGH`
160	- Acknowledge: `POST /alerts/<id>/ack`
161	- Resolve: `POST /alerts/<id>/resolve`
162	
163	## 6. Environment Variables Reference
164	
165	All configuration flows through `src/config/__init__.py`. Key security settings:
166	
167	| Variable | Default | Description |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| `SECRET_KEY` | change-me | Flask secret key |
170	| `JWT_SECRET_KEY` | change-me | JWT signing key |
171	| `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` | change-me | AES-256-GCM master key |
172	| `REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET` | change-me | HMAC request signing key |
173	| `ENABLE_TLS` | true | Enforce HTTPS |
174	| `LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` | 5 | Lockout threshold |
175	| `CAPTCHA_THRESHOLD` | 3 | CAPTCHA trigger threshold |
176	| `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE` | 60 | Rate limiter tokens/minute |
177	| `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS` | 14 | Backup file retention |
178	| `HOLD_EXPIRY_MINUTES` | 10 | Reservation hold TTL |
179	
180	**All `change-me` values MUST be replaced in production.**
181	
182	## 7. Monitoring Checklist
183	
184	| Check | Method | Frequency |
185	|---|---|---|
186	| Service health | `GET /health` | Every 30 seconds (load balancer) |
187	| Database connectivity | Health endpoint `database` field | Every 30 seconds |
188	| Disk usage (data, exports, backups) | `docker system df`, volume inspection | Daily |
189	| Open alerts | `GET /alerts?status=OPEN` | Continuously (dashboard) |
190	| Audit event volume | `GET /audit-events` with date range | Weekly review |
191	| System status | `GET /admin/system-status` (platform admin) | Daily |
192	| TLS certificate expiry | External cert checker | Weekly |
193	| Backup file presence | `ls /app/backups/*.db` | Daily |
194	
195	## 8. Shutdown and Maintenance
196	
197	### Graceful shutdown
198	```
199	docker compose stop api
200	```
201	
202	### Full teardown (preserves volumes)
203	```
204	docker compose down
205	```
206	
207	### Full teardown including data
208	```
209	docker compose down -v
210	```
211	Warning: This destroys all database, export, and backup data.

13	def verify_request_signature(request) -> tuple:
14	    """Verify the signature, timestamp, and nonce of an incoming request.
15	
16	    Expects headers:
17	        X-Timestamp: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the request was signed.
18	        X-Nonce: Unique nonce to prevent replay attacks.
19	        X-Signature: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of "method:path:timestamp:nonce:body_hash".
20	
21	    Args:
22	        request: The Flask request object.
23	
24	    Returns:
25	        Tuple of (is_valid: bool, error_code: str or None).
26	        Error codes: MISSING_SIGNATURE_HEADERS, TIMESTAMP_EXPIRED,
27	                     NONCE_REPLAYED, INVALID_SIGNATURE.
28	    """
29	    timestamp = request.headers.get("X-Timestamp")
30	    nonce = request.headers.get("X-Nonce")
31	    signature = request.headers.get("X-Signature")
32	
33	    if not timestamp or not nonce or not signature:
34	        logger.warning("security", "signing", "Missing signature headers")
35	        return False, "MISSING_SIGNATURE_HEADERS"
36	
37	    # Check timestamp skew
38	    try:
39	        request_time = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp)
40	        if request_time.tzinfo is None:
41	            request_time = request_time.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
42	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
43	        logger.warning("security", "signing", f"Invalid timestamp format: {timestamp}")
44	        return False, "TIMESTAMP_EXPIRED"
45	
46	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
47	    skew = timedelta(seconds=config.REQUEST_SIGNING_SKEW_SECONDS)
48	    if abs(now - request_time) > skew:
49	        logger.warning("security", "signing", "Request timestamp outside allowed skew")
50	        return False, "TIMESTAMP_EXPIRED"
51	
52	    # Check nonce replay
53	    existing_nonce = NonceStore.query.filter_by(nonce=nonce).first()
54	    if existing_nonce:
55	        logger.warning("security", "signing", f"Nonce replayed: {nonce}")
56	        return False, "NONCE_REPLAYED"
57	
58	    # Compute expected signature
59	    body = request.get_data()
60	    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
61	    method = request.method.upper()
62	    path = request.path
63	
64	    message = f"{method}:{path}:{timestamp}:{nonce}:{body_hash}"
65	    expected = hmac.new(
66	        config.REQUEST_SIGNING_SECRET.encode("utf-8"),
67	        message.encode("utf-8"),
68	        hashlib.sha256,
69	    ).hexdigest()
70	
71	    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):
72	        logger.warning("security", "signing", "Invalid request signature")
73	        return False, "INVALID_SIGNATURE"
74	
75	    # Store nonce to prevent replay
76	    nonce_record = NonceStore(
77	        nonce=nonce,
78	        expires_at=now + timedelta(seconds=config.NONCE_RETENTION_SECONDS),
79	    )
80	    db.session.add(nonce_record)
81	    db.session.commit()
82	
83	    logger.debug("security", "signing", "Request signature verified successfully")
84	    return True, None

class TestTLSEnforcement:
    """Test the TLS enforcement middleware function directly."""

    def test_rejects_http_when_tls_enabled(self, app, db):
        """When ENABLE_TLS is true the before_request hook must reject non-HTTPS."""
        from src.config import config

        original = config.ENABLE_TLS
        try:
            config.ENABLE_TLS = True
            # Build a non-testing app to avoid the TESTING bypass
            test_app = create_app(testing=False)

            test_app.config["TESTING"] = False

                # so TLS enforcement should reject it.
                assert resp.status_code == 403
                body = resp.get_json()
                assert body["error"]["code"] == "TLS_REQUIRED"

            config.ENABLE_TLS = original
